Issued at 232 AM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

Fall has finally arrived to the area. Sunday was the coolest day may 
locations have seen since May. And it looks like we are through with 
the record high temperatures for a while, although we should see 
some moderation in temperatures toward seasonal normals toward the 
end of the week.

The moisture from Rachel that moved over the area today is now 
moving away to the north and east. We still have some showers across 
the area, although most of the precipitation is on the light side. 
Notice how I said precipitation though. There has been some snow in 
the mountains. And even in the lower elevations, we have seen some 
mixing in places like Cody and Powell, although there have been no 
reported problems with roads. The general trend should be down 
through the night, although some rain and mountain snow will linger 
until morning.

Our attention now turns away from the moisture from Rachel to that 
big bowling ball to west, AKA an upper level now swirling over 
Oregon. This feature has been giving me fits over the details of 
its direction, and, most importantly, the ultimate impacts of the 
weather across western and central Wyoming. And the good news is we 
finally have somewhat better agreement in the path of it. The models 
are digging the low a bit further south, both the operational GFS 
and European models, as well as a majority of the ensemble members 
dig the low further south, moving across the Great Basin to near Las 
Vegas by Tuesday evening. The result at this point looks to be 
somewhat less precipitation. There should be somewhat of a lull this 
morning as we will be in between systems. There are some indications 
of a weak meso low that may try to move into the area, but the 
models are split on this. Nevertheless, the majority of the showers 
will fall West of the Divide today, especially during the day. 
Northeastern portions of the County Warning Area may have a mainly 
dry day today. Another wave should bring an increase in showers 
tonight. However, there is a decent spread of where the most 
numerous showers will fall. And it will be a cool day as well, with 
below normal temperatures. As for precipitation amounts, I will talk 
about those in separate paragraphs further down. As for the high 
wind warning, we will let it ride until expiration. We will let
the freeze warning ride for now. And, with the cold comes snow.
We will also discuss that in another paragraph.

Tuesday looks like a similar day with cool temperatures and most of 
the showers across southern and western Wyoming with fewer further 
to the north. The low will begin to make a turn toward the northeast 
Tuesday night and into Wednesday. This is when the wettest period 
should be for areas East of the Divide as flow turns more easterly, 
bring an upslope component. It should be noted though that with the 
low further to the south, we will closer to the edge of the moisture 
so precipitation amounts have been cut, to about half of what they 
were yesterday at this time. Showers should linger into Wednesday 
before gradually ending as we head into Thursday as the low moves 
away. Which way it moves depends on what model you believe, but most 
agree it will move away. Dry weather should then return Friday and 
into the weekend as flow turns zonal as flat ridging builds, bring a 
return to near normal temperatures.

PRECIPITATION AMOUNTS...I will break this up into two different 
segments. The first will be the twenty four hours through tonight. 
No surprise, the highest amounts will be across western and southern 
Wyoming, with the 1 out of 2 chance line roughly running south of a 
Jackson to Casper line. The chance of a half an inch or more is 
generally 1 out 2 across the southwestern quarter of the state. The 
epicenter is, no surprise across the western slopes of the Wind 
River Range were where is a 1 out of 2 chance of an inch or more. 
Amounts decrease further north where many areas may end up with a 
mainly dry day. As for Tuesday through Wednesday night, all areas 
have at least a 1 in 2 chance of a quarter of an inch or 
precipitation, south of a Jackson to Buffalo line as the main 
concern for precipitation shifts to central and southern Wyoming. 
When we bump it up to an inch, the main concern switches to the east 
to northeasterly upslope locations East of the Divide, mainly 
along and south of US 20 26 from Dubois to Casper, with lesser 
amounts across western Wyoming as the upper level low moves 
further to the east. Some locations, especially the Wind River 
Range have the potential to pick up an additional two inches of 
QPF by Thursday morning.

SNOWFALL...Snow level at this time are generally running between 
8000 and 8500 feet this morning in central Wyoming to around 7000
feet in northern Wyoming in regards to accumulating snow. Through 
the day today, snow levels should remain in in this vicinity so
